result:
Both integrate one branch's changes into another; difference is history shape.

`git merge feature`: creates merge commit with two parents, tying histories together. Existing commits untouched → safe on shared branches, true record of what happened. Cost: non-linear graph, noisy with frequent merges. (Fast-forward when no divergence → no merge commit.)

`git rebase main`: replays your commits one by one on top of `main` as new commits with new SHAs. Linear history, cleaner `git log`/`bisect`. Cost: rewrites history → rebasing already-pushed commits others have based work on breaks their branches and needs a force push (`--force-with-lease`). Conflicts get resolved per replayed commit, not once.

Rule: rebase local/unshared work to tidy it up, merge into shared branches. Common flow: `git rebase main` on feature branch, then merge the feature into `main`.
